_comment: Per-culture jealousy norms for Calradia Remembers. Entries live under 'cultures', keyed by culture DISPLAY NAME (same convention as cultural_traditions.json) so faction/conversion mods can add or override entries without touching code. Any culture absent from this file falls back to a strictly monogamous profile (High exclusivity, no shared partners) — the conservative default. Fields (all optional; omitted fields take the monogamous default): exclusivityOutrage = High|Medium|Low (how strongly a liaison elsewhere reads as betrayal); polygamyEliteTier = minimum clan tier 0..6 at/above which sharing partners is culturally tolerated (below it the culture behaves monogamously; use 0 for 'always tolerated', leave high/omit for monogamous); hierarchySensitivity = High|Medium|Low (how strongly senior-vs-secondary partner rank drives competition jealousy); equityExpectation = true when the offence is UNEQUAL treatment rather than rank itself; promptHint = one-sentence cultural framing injected into the jealous party's reaction.

Vlandia.promptHint: Your people hold marriage sacred and to one alone; a love given elsewhere is a betrayal of your honour and your house.

Empire.promptHint: By the customs of the Empire a bond is between two; to be set aside for another is a public humiliation, not a thing to be borne quietly.

Sturgia.promptHint: Your people prize loyalty above all; a partner who gives their heart elsewhere has broken faith, and that is not forgiven lightly.

Battania.promptHint: Among the highborn of your people a chief may take more than one spouse, but the first wife's standing is hers by right — and she may refuse to share her hall, or leave.

Khuzait.promptHint: Among your people a powerful figure may keep several spouses; there is a senior wife whose children inherit and the others rank beneath her. Your grievance is rank and primacy, not the sharing itself.

Aserai.promptHint: Your customs permit several wives, but each must be treated with equal honour; the wound is in being slighted or neglected, not in being one of several.

Nords.promptHint: Your jarls may keep several wives or concubines, yet a strong partner will not be treated as property nor set below another without cause.
